symbols.name: N
symbols.def: Number of fixed experimental units, restricted to multiples of \(K\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Cut location in the ordered unit list.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Generic scalarization direction for the contrast vector.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: Prespecified positive-semidefinite scalarization of contrast covariance.

symbols.name: \bar Y
symbols.def: Armwise finite-population mean with coordinate \(\bar Y(a)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i(a)\).

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: Collection \(F=(F_a)_{a\in\mathcal A}\) of equal-weight empirical armwise marginals.

symbols.name: \mathcal S_N(F)
symbols.def: All fixed \(N\)-row schedules with armwise empirical marginals \(F\).

symbols.name: S(Y)
symbols.def: Finite-population covariance matrix with \(S_{ab}(Y)=(N-1)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\{Y_i(a)-\bar Y(a)\}\{Y_i(b)-\bar Y(b)\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\bar Y}
symbols.def: Observed arm-mean vector with coordinate \(\widehat{\bar Y}(a)=n^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_i=a}Y_i(a)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal R_K
symbols.def: Graph-Laplacian rank cone \(\mathcal R_K=\{G\in\mathbb S_+^K:G\mathbf 1_K=0,\ G_{ab}\leq0\text{ for all }a\neq b\}\).

symbols.name: \Omega
symbols.def: Candidate assignment covariance tensor with coordinate \(\Omega_{abij}\) indexed by arms \(a,b\) and units \(i,j\); admissibility is defined by the exact balanced-law moment representation below.

symbols.name: \mathcal Z_{N,K}
symbols.def: Fixed-count allocation space \(\mathcal Z_{N,K}=\{z\in\mathcal A^N:\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf 1(z_i=a)=n\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal A\}\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Probability mass function on the fixed-count allocation space.

symbols.name: \mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}
symbols.def: Balanced assignment-law polytope defined by fixed allocation counts and unitwise arm marginals \(1/K\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}
symbols.def: Image of \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\) under the centered assignment-covariance moment map.

symbols.name: \pi
symbols.def: Common relabelling of the experimental units.

symbols.name: [\Omega]_{\cong}
symbols.def: Orbit \([\Omega]_{\cong}=\{\Omega^{\pi}:\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\}\) under common unit relabelling.

symbols.name: x
symbols.def: Ordered arm columns \(x=(x^a)_{a\in\mathcal A}\), one for each empirical marginal.

symbols.name: \mathscr L_{H,\Omega}(x,\sigma)
symbols.def: Kernel covariance loss obtained by assigning ordered arm column \(x^a\) through \(\sigma_a\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{N,K}(H)
symbols.def: Universal identity-optimal cone for the kernel loss at contrast Gram matrix \(H\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)
symbols.def: Admissible balanced rank-preserving kernel classes whose unit-relabeling orbit meets \(\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\).

assumptions.condition: The assignment \(Z\) is uniform over all allocations satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf 1(Z_i=a)=n\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).

definitions.name: Universal rank-preservation cone
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R_K=\{G\in\mathbb S_+^K:G\mathbf 1_K=0,\ G_{ab}\leq0\text{ for every }a\neq b\}\).

definitions.name: Valid balanced assignment laws
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}=\{p\in\Delta(\mathcal Z_{N,K}):\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z_{N,K}}p(z)\mathbf 1(z_i=a)=K^{-1}\text{ for every }i\text{ and }a\}\). Thus every law has the fixed counts encoded by \(\mathcal Z_{N,K}\), total mass one, nonnegative atom probabilities, and marginal probabilities \(\Pr_p(Z_i=a)=1/K\), but no unit-exchangeability or arm-exchangeability restriction.

definitions.name: Admissible balanced covariance tensors
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}=\left\{\Omega:\exists p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K},\quad \Omega_{abij}=\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z_{N,K}}p(z)\{K\mathbf 1(z_i=a)-1\}\{K\mathbf 1(z_j=b)-1\}\right\}.\] This finite moment-polytope representation is the exact feasibility constraint. Every member satisfies the covariance symmetry \(\Omega_{abij}=\Omega_{baji}\); the arm-sum identities \(\sum_a\Omega_{abij}=\sum_b\Omega_{abij}=0\); the fixed-count unit-sum identities \(\sum_i\Omega_{abij}=\sum_j\Omega_{abij}=0\); the same-unit identities \(\Omega_{aaii}=K-1\) and \(\Omega_{abii}=-1\) for \(a\neq b\); the bounds \(-1\leq\Omega_{abij}\leq K-1\); and positive semidefiniteness of the \(NK\times NK\) matrix indexed by \((a,i)\). No further permutation symmetry is imposed, and the listed identities without the displayed probability-simplex representation are not taken as sufficient for feasibility.

definitions.name: Equivalence of balanced kernels under unit relabelling
definitions.construction: For \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\), define \((\Omega^{\pi})_{abij}=\Omega_{ab,\pi(i),\pi(j)}\). Write \(\Omega\cong\Omega'\) exactly when \(\Omega'=\Omega^{\pi}\) for some \(\pi\), and set \([\Omega]_{\cong}=\{\Omega^{\pi}:\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\}\).

definitions.name: Balanced-kernel covariance loss
definitions.construction: For \(x\in\mathcal M_N^K\) and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\), \[\mathscr L_{H,\Omega}(x,\sigma)=\frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}\sum_{i,j=1}^N H_{ab}\Omega_{abij}x^a_{\sigma_a(i)}x^b_{\sigma_b(j)}.\] If \(\Omega\) is induced by \(p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), this equals \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_p(C\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)\}\) for the schedule having arm columns \(x^a\circ\sigma_a\).

definitions.name: Universal identity-optimal tensor cone
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)=\left\{\Omega\in\mathbb R^{K\times K\times N\times N}:\mathscr L_{H,\Omega}(x,\mathrm{id})\geq\mathscr L_{H,\Omega}(x,\sigma)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal M_N^K\text{ and }\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\right\}.\] It is a closed convex cone because every defining comparison is homogeneous and linear in \(\Omega\).

definitions.name: Admissible rank-preserving kernel classes
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)=\left\{[\Omega]_{\cong}:\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K},\ [\Omega]_{\cong}\cap\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\neq\varnothing\right\}.\] Recognition is posed only for an input tensor already in the feasible domain \(\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\); equivalently, the input may include a valid law \(p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\) that induces it.

definitions.name: Cut-generator handle for general assignment kernels
definitions.construction: Starting move: for each \(x^a\in\mathcal M_N\), use \(x^a=x^a_1\mathbf 1_N+\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}(x^a_{r+1}-x^a_r)d_r\); insert these nonnegative adjacent increments into \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega}\), quotient by \([\Omega]_{\cong}\), and seek a finite cut-product separation certificate for membership in \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\).

statements.statement: Under balanced complete randomization, \[\Sigma_C(Y)=C\left\{\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}{N}\right\}C^{\mathsf T}\] and hence \[\rho_W(Y)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{H_{aa}S_{aa}(Y)}{n}-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y).\] Therefore all completion dependence is carried by the off-diagonal cross-arm covariances.
statements.justification: This identity exposes the exact coefficients multiplying the unidentified cross-world covariances.
statements.gap: Zhao and Ding state the covariance formula for arbitrary contrasts but do not use it to solve the least-favourable completion problem.
statements.consumer: It converts a multi-arm causal-bootstrap integer program into a contrast-geometry diagnostic whenever pairwise rearrangement is valid.

statements.statement: The following are equivalent. First, for every balanced size \(N\) divisible by \(2K\) and every collection \(F\) of equal-weight empirical armwise marginals, \[Y^{\uparrow}(F)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)}\rho_W(Y).\] Second, \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\in\mathcal R_K\). When these conditions hold, the exact regret identity is \[\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)=\frac{2}{N}\sum_{a<b}(-H_{ab})\left[S_{ab}\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-S_{ab}(Y)\right]\geq0.\] If \(H_{ab}>0\) for some pair, binary marginals that vary only in arms \(a\) and \(b\) give a finite balanced counterexample in which common ranks are strictly suboptimal.
statements.justification: The theorem gives a necessary-and-sufficient, polynomially checkable boundary for universal least-favourable rank completion.
statements.gap: Aronow, Green, and Lee cover one two-arm ray; Brennan et al. and Gao, Ge, and Qian compute general endpoints but do not identify this universal design-induced cone.
statements.consumer: A multi-arm causal-bootstrap implementation can replace integer optimization by one sort exactly when the reported contrast loss lies in \(\mathcal R_K\).

statements.statement: For a nonzero contrast matrix \(C\), the positive-semidefinite dominance \[\Sigma_C\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}\succeq\Sigma_C(Y)\quad\text{for every }N\text{ divisible by }2K,F,\text{ and }Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)\] holds if and only if all columns of \(C\) vanish except two columns that are negatives of one another. Equivalently, every nonzero universally Loewner-dominated multi-contrast system is a vector rescaling of one pairwise arm contrast. For any other \(C\), there is a direction \(h\) and binary armwise marginals for which common ranking reduces \(\operatorname{Var}_Z(h^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau)\).
statements.justification: Scalar risk optimality does not imply joint covariance conservativeness; this theorem identifies the exact and unexpectedly narrow boundary.
statements.gap: No located causal-bootstrap or multi-arm design paper classifies when one completed science table dominates the full covariance matrix for all marginal schedules.
statements.consumer: Analysts constructing simultaneous Wald regions learn when a single rank-preserving bootstrap covariance is valid and when contrast-specific completion is unavoidable.

statements.statement: When \(K=2\), \(m=1\), \(C=(-1,1)\), and \(W=(1)\), the cone condition holds and \(Y^{\uparrow}(F)\) yields exactly the comonotone sharp upper randomization-variance endpoint of Aronow, Green, and Lee.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check against the canonical sharp two-arm result.
statements.gap: This proposition is intentionally an equivalence check rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Existing two-arm causal-bootstrap software becomes a verified special case of the general certificate.

statements.statement: If the rows of \(C\) form an orthonormal basis of the zero-sum contrast space and \(W\) is the identity matrix, then \(H_{aa}=1-K^{-1}\) and \(H_{ab}=-K^{-1}\) for \(a\neq b\), so \(H\in\mathcal R_K\). Thus common ranks maximize the sum of the randomization variances of a complete orthonormal contrast system, even though Theorem 3 rules out universal Loewner dominance when \(K>2\).
statements.justification: This nondegenerate multi-arm case separates a valid omnibus scalarization from invalid joint covariance dominance.
statements.gap: Zhao and Ding permit complete contrast systems but do not derive their sharp common-rank covariance-loss endpoint.
statements.consumer: Factorial and analysis-of-variance designs obtain an analytic least-favourable total-variance benchmark.

statements.statement: Fix \(N\), \(K\), and \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\), and restrict the input to a rational tensor \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), supplied either with its exact entries or by a rational law \(p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\) inducing those entries. Characterize the cone \(\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\) on this feasible domain and hence the label-free set \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\): equivalently, decide whether some common unit relabelling \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) makes \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\mathrm{id})\geq\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\sigma)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal M_N^K\) and every \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\). Derive a recognition algorithm polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and the rational input bit length that returns such a relabelling and a finite cut certificate on yes instances, and returns arm-specific binary ordered columns together with \(\sigma\) giving a strict exact loss improvement on no instances; if binary separation is not complete, characterize the minimal finite alphabet required for a complete separating certificate.
statements.justification: The feasible moment-polytope domain separates genuine randomization kernels from arbitrary four-index arrays and turns universal rank preservation into a label-invariant decision problem.
statements.gap: Brennan et al. solve feasible design instances numerically, while Laurent and Seminaroti give a sufficient Robinson--Toeplitz identity-optimal class for a two-matrix quadratic assignment problem rather than a necessary-and-sufficient certificate over balanced assignment-law covariance tensors.
statements.consumer: Designers of matched, paired, rerandomized, and geographically balanced experiments receive a certificate tied to a realizable assignment law, or an exact finite completion showing why rank-preserving imputation fails.

statements.statement: For the balanced experiment with \(K=3\), \(N=6\), \(n=2\), \(m=2\), \[C=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&0\\0&1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad W=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad H=C^{\mathsf T}WC=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&0\\-1&2&-1\\0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}\in\mathcal R_3.\] Let every arm marginal put mass \(1/2\) on zero and \(1/2\) on one. The common-rank schedule has every column equal to \((0,0,0,1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), satisfies \(S_{ab}=3/10\) for all \(a,b\), and has \(\rho_W=3/5\). The feasible schedule \(Y\) with columns \((0,0,0,1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), \((1,1,1,0,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\), and \((0,0,0,1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\) has \(S_{12}=S_{23}=-3/10\), \(S_{13}=3/10\), and \(\rho_W(Y)=1/5\). Thus the exact graph-Laplacian regret certificate is \[\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)=\frac{1}{3}\left\{\frac{3}{10}-\left(-\frac{3}{10}\right)+\frac{3}{10}-\left(-\frac{3}{10}\right)\right\}=\frac{2}{5}.\]
statements.justification: This finite certificate makes the sufficient graph-Laplacian mechanism and every covariance-loss arithmetic step directly auditable.
statements.gap: The general supermodular-order argument does not display the induced multi-contrast risk coefficients or a fully evaluated multi-arm finite-population example.
statements.consumer: A causal-bootstrap implementation obtains a six-unit regression test whose exact answer detects sign, normalization, and factor-of-two errors in the cone certificate.

statements.statement: For the balanced experiment with \(K=3\), \(N=6\), \(n=2\), \(m=1\), \(C=(1,1,-2)\), and \(W=(1)\), \[H=C^{\mathsf T}WC=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&-2\\1&1&-2\\-2&-2&4\end{pmatrix}\notin\mathcal R_3\] because \(H_{12}=1>0\). Let \(F_1=F_2=\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac12\delta_1\) and \(F_3=\delta_0\). Common ranking uses columns \((0,0,0,1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), \((0,0,0,1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), and zero, so \(S_{11}=S_{22}=S_{12}=3/10\) and \(\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}=1/10\). Reversing only the second binary column gives a feasible \(Y\) with \(S_{11}=S_{22}=3/10\), \(S_{12}=-3/10\), and \(\rho_W(Y)=3/10\). Consequently \[\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)=\frac{1}{3}(-1)\left\{\frac{3}{10}-\left(-\frac{3}{10}\right)\right\}=-\frac{1}{5},\] an exact binary certificate of strict common-rank failure.
statements.justification: The witness exposes the necessity mechanism with a valid contrast Gram matrix, isolated binary margins, and exact finite-sample losses.
statements.gap: Classical rearrangement results imply how a signed pair behaves but do not identify this non-Laplacian causal contrast or evaluate its complete-randomization loss.
statements.consumer: Software checking \(H_{ab}\leq0\) can return this exact three-arm counterexample template whenever it detects a positive off-diagonal coefficient.

sampling_model.design: The headline theorems use balanced complete randomization, uniform over assignments with exactly \(n=N/K\) units in each arm. The open kernel problem ranges only over laws in \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\): every realized allocation has those fixed counts and every unit has marginal arm probability \(1/K\), without exchangeability.
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) units and all \(K\) potential outcomes per unit are fixed; there is no super-population sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The assignment vector \(Z\) is the sole random object and is generated by the known complete-randomization law or the known admissible nonexchangeable law \(p\).
sampling_model.overlap: Each arm has known marginal assignment probability \(1/K\) and a positive fixed allocation count.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The identification theorem conditions on the armwise empirical marginal laws \(F\); empirical estimation of those margins is outside the first structural kernel and follows the quantile plug-in route of Aronow, Green, and Lee.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The upper bound is attained if the two potential outcomes are comonotonic.
An integer program computes a worst-case copula for broad designs and estimators.
Multi-marginal optimal transport gives exact identified sets for general quadratic cross-world objectives.
The design-based framework permits arbitrary multi-arm contrast matrices.
Supermodular expectations are monotone in concordance for distributions with fixed marginals.
The identity permutation is optimal for a Robinson similarity and dissimilarity when one is Toeplitz.
Isotone imputation converges to a least-favourable two-arm limiting experiment.

tldr: Under balanced complete randomization, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) if and only if the contrast Gram matrix \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian. This yields an \(O(K^2)\) certificate, an exact \(K=3,N=6\) worked calculation, and an explicit binary counterexample outside the cone. A second exact boundary shows that common ranks dominate the entire multi-contrast covariance matrix only for a rescaled single pairwise contrast. The open research step characterizes identity-optimality only among covariance tensors induced by valid fixed-count, marginally balanced assignment laws, modulo common unit relabelling, and seeks a polynomial cut certificate with an exact failure witness.

project_justification.gap: Sharp rank completion is analytic for the two-arm difference-in-means estimator, whereas generalized causal-bootstrap work uses integer programming for broad designs and estimators. The literature does not state the exact contrast-geometry boundary at which one common-rank completion remains universally least favourable in a multi-arm experiment, nor a label-invariant recognition problem restricted to realizable nonexchangeable balanced covariance kernels.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator. It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone for complete randomization, a stronger classification for joint covariance dominance, and an admissible moment-polytope domain on which the nonexchangeable recognition problem has statistical meaning.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the complete-randomization risk decomposition, proves the graph-Laplacian iff theorem by pairwise rearrangement and isolated binary necessity witnesses, evaluates both mechanisms exactly at \(K=3,N=6\), classifies the Loewner case, and uses cut generators to characterize the identity-optimal cone over covariance tensors induced by valid balanced assignment laws modulo unit relabelling.

related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee establish the two-arm comonotone sharp endpoint; Proposition 4 recovers that result exactly. Imbens and Menzel use the same isotone completion to obtain a least-favourable limiting experiment. Zhao and Ding supply the arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance identity used in Lemma 1 but do not optimize its unidentified cross-arm terms. Tchen's supermodular-order theorem supplies the pairwise rearrangement ingredient, so the proposal does not claim a new general dependence inequality. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, while Brennan et al. compute generalized causal-bootstrap completions by integer programming; both inform the search for a certificate that avoids instance-specific optimization. The open problem takes as its domain only covariance tensors in the exact finite moment-polytope image of balanced assignment laws, rather than arbitrary quadratic-program coefficient arrays. Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz quadratic-assignment theorem supplies the cut-decomposition model for this open nonexchangeable-kernel extension, not a theorem-level result that the present proposal claims to sharpen.
technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate concerns a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\). It does not turn that scalar endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued covariance bound. Theorem 3 makes this distinction formal: except for a rescaled pairwise contrast, no single common-rank completion can dominate every linear combination simultaneously.
honest_scope: The complete-randomization cone theorem should be attainable by combining the published covariance identity with rearrangement and a new necessity classification; its novelty is the causal contrast geometry and Loewner boundary, not the underlying supermodular inequality. The \(K=3,N=6\) propositions are exact audit certificates rather than additional asymptotic claims. The assignment-kernel characterization in Open-ended Question 6 is the first-class unresolved component and is posed only for covariance tensors induced by valid fixed-count, marginally balanced laws, modulo common unit relabelling. Whether every failure in that feasible domain has a binary separator is part of the open question. The proposal does not claim finite-sample tail dominance, empirical-marginal inference, or a closed form outside the certified cone.

seed_details.seed: Graph-Laplacian rank cone and Loewner boundary
seed_details.anchor_read: Aronow, Green, and Lee were read at the Introduction, Section 3, Lemma 1 and its proof, equations (7)--(11), and the Discussion. Brennan et al. were read at the Introduction, the quadratic variance formulation, the integer program in equation (4), Theorem 1 and its proof architecture, and the Conclusion.
seed_details.live_opportunity: The two-arm comonotone endpoint is analytic, while the generalized causal bootstrap resorts to instance-specific integer optimization. The missing object is the exact multi-contrast matrix cone on which one common-rank completion is universally least favourable.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the scalar Hoeffding covariance term by the complete-randomization identity for \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\), then test whether every pairwise covariance deficit has a nonnegative coefficient.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for multi-arm sharp covariance bounds, universal comonotone quadratic objectives, and rank-preserving causal bootstrap contrast matrices found general supermodular-order results and computational multi-marginal transport, but no causal graph-Laplacian or Loewner classification.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Tchen because a quadratic objective is supermodular exactly when its cross-partials are nonnegative.
seed_details.rebuttal: Tchen supplies the extremal-order ingredient, not the design-to-cost reduction, the exact contrast-risk cone \(C^{\mathsf T}WC\), or the classification showing that universal positive-semidefinite covariance dominance collapses to one pairwise contrast.

seed_details.seed: Cut-cone certificate for nonexchangeable balanced designs
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, the assignment-covariance quadratic form, equation (4), Sections 4--5, Theorem 1 with its feasibility proof, and the Conclusion were read.
seed_details.live_opportunity: Brennan et al. make general design-specific completion problems computationally accessible but leave open when a covariance tensor induced by a valid fixed-count, marginally balanced assignment law admits one universally optimal rank ordering.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Map the exact polytope of fixed-count, marginally balanced assignment laws into its covariance-tensor image, quotient that image by common unit relabellings, and reduce universal completion optimality to simultaneous quadratic-assignment inequalities over ordered arm columns.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for rank-preserving completion with realizable randomization kernels and for universal identity-optimal quadratic assignment found Robinson--Toeplitz sufficient classes, but not a necessary-and-sufficient certificate on the balanced assignment-law moment polytope.
seed_details.red_team: This is merely the Robinsonian quadratic-assignment theorem under causal notation.
seed_details.rebuttal: The causal problem is multi-block, permits several arm permutations, restricts coefficient tensors to those induced by valid balanced assignment laws, factors out common unit relabellings, and asks necessity over every ordered marginal vector; the Robinson--Toeplitz theorem is a sufficient two-matrix identity-optimal result and explicitly fails without its Toeplitz restriction.

seed_details.seed: Dual-tight hypergraph certificate for zero realization loss
seed_details.anchor_read: The banked proposal's project justification, variance certificate, open question, and reviewer strengthening path were read. Gao, Ge, and Qian were read at the Introduction, Section 2, Theorem 1 and its proof sketch, the quadratic extension, and the Discussion.
seed_details.live_opportunity: The banked proposal proves only a rate for converting fractional multi-marginal plans into common-row finite populations; it does not decide when the conversion is exact.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After transport duality identifies the tight support face, replace approximate hierarchical repair by an integrality test for the incidence matrix of that face.
seed_details.destination_search: The adjacent search found non-Monge extreme-point geometry and discrete quadratic transport, but no polynomial iff certificate for an \(N\)-row optimizer on an arbitrary dual-tight face.
seed_details.red_team: Zero gap is equivalent by definition to an integer feasible point on the tight face.
seed_details.rebuttal: The publishable content would be a structural and polynomially checkable characterization, such as balanced hypergraph or total-unimodularity geometry, not the tautological integer-feasibility restatement.

seed_details.seed: Residual rank cone for regression-adjusted multi-arm experiments
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Section 4.2 on out-of-sample regression residuals, the general quadratic program, the asymptotic theorem, and the Conclusion were read.
seed_details.live_opportunity: Regression adjustment changes the armwise objects from outcomes to residuals, while existing work computes sharp endpoints without a universal contrast-geometry certificate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Substitute predictable residual schedules into the complete-randomization covariance decomposition and determine whether the same graph-Laplacian condition survives arm-specific residualization.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found sharp two-arm regression-residual bounds but no multi-arm universal rank cone.
seed_details.red_team: This follows verbatim by replacing outcomes with residuals.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection holds for fixed out-of-sample residuals, so the seed lacks an independent kernel unless adjustment is estimated under the realized assignment.

Imbens and Menzel were read at the Introduction, causal-bootstrap construction, least-favourable limiting experiment, Lemma 1 and Proposition 1 proofs based on convex order, and the large-sample coverage argument.
seed_details.live_opportunity: Worst variance and asymptotic least favourability do not determine rejection probabilities of a studentized statistic in finite populations.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The convex-order proof for the unstudentized estimator fails when the random denominator changes with the completion; the replacement target is exact randomization-tail optimization.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for studentized causal-bootstrap tail dominance found asymptotic and Edgeworth refinements, not finite-sample dominance over completions.
seed_details.red_team: Variance maximization plus symmetry already implies the widest tails.
seed_details.rebuttal: Studentization destroys that implication, and Brennan et al.'s finite example shows that worst-variance completion need not yield conservative small-sample coverage.
seed_details.disposition: dropped after ranking because the exact optimizer is likely critical-value specific

seed_details.seed: Sharp covariance deficit under a rank-discordance budget
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Section 3, the Hoeffding lemma and proof, the quantile estimator, and the Discussion were read.
seed_details.live_opportunity: The sharp endpoint jumps directly to comonotonicity and does not quantify variance loss when rank preservation is substantively implausible.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the unrestricted Fr\'{e}chet class in the Hoeffding proof by a copula slice with fixed Kendall dependence or bounded discordant mass.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found treatment-effect-distribution bounds under dependence information, but not a closed covariance-deficit frontier for randomization variance.
seed_details.red_team: This is a standard constrained-copula optimization with no causal content.
seed_details.rebuttal: The exact critical dependence level for a design-variance conclusion and its finite-population realization would be causal and operational, but the nonlinear copula slice makes feasibility uncertain.

seed_details.anchor_read: The banked proposal's TLDR, transport constructions, variance certificate, exact-constant open question, README, and reviewer objections were read.
seed_details.live_opportunity: The existing proposal leaves the limit of \(N\Delta_N\) and the extremal dual-tight geometry unresolved.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace separate multiscale upper and padded-obstruction lower bounds by a compactness or arithmetic classification of all asymptotically tight support faces.
seed_details.destination_search: The adjacent search found non-Monge and mixability geometry but no exact same-denominator causal completion constant.
seed_details.red_team: The normalized gap may oscillate arithmetically, so there is no single constant to estimate.
seed_details.rebuttal: The honest target can be the exact subsequential-limit set, but the required face classification is substantially less feasible than the rank-cone certificate.

seed_details.seed: History-tree gluing of nodewise rank extrema
seed_details.anchor_read: The failed proposal's completion class and open question, the angle review's well-posedness objection, and the recommended history-tree repair were read.
seed_details.live_opportunity: A legal adaptive design requires one ex ante potential-outcome table, whereas rectangular nodewise optimization chooses incompatible couplings across histories.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace nodewise coupling feasibility by a projective-consistency problem over the entire observed-history tree before applying martingale variance decomposition.
seed_details.destination_search: The targeted prior-art review found adaptive martingale inference and static transport envelopes, but no global completion theorem.
seed_details.red_team: This is ordinary marginal consistency on a finite tree and follows from a gluing lemma.
seed_details.rebuttal: The same labelled units and history-dependent residual maps impose nonrectangular constraints not covered by ordinary pairwise gluing, but even defining the feasible object cleanly remains difficult.

seed_details.seed: Sign-switched rank completion for a single multi-arm contrast
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, multi-marginal formulation, quadratic objective, Theorem 1 and proof sketch, minimax proposition, and Discussion were read.
seed_details.live_opportunity: A scalar contrast with several positive and negative coefficients suggests sorting arms in two opposite rank groups rather than using common ranks.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Apply sign changes to the quadratic contrast cost and check the compatibility of all mixed partials before invoking the comonotone optimizer.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found the compatible-cost or sign-switched supermodularity theorem in multi-marginal risk aggregation.
seed_details.red_team: The optimizer is already the standard compatible-cost comonotone coupling after changing signs.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds, so this seed is not novel even though it gives a useful causal corollary.

literature_map.settled: Aronow, Green, and Lee prove that the comonotone coupling attains the sharp upper covariance and variance endpoint for two-arm difference-in-means under fixed marginals.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their statement does not classify scalarized covariance risks or positive-semidefinite covariance dominance for a general multi-arm contrast matrix.
literature_map.locator: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Introduction, Section 3, Lemma 1, equations (7)--(11), and Discussion.

literature_map.settled: Brennan et al. formulate worst-case completion as an integer program for broad known designs and linear- or quadratic-in-treatment estimators and prove asymptotic feasibility coverage.
literature_map.open_boundary: The program is instance-specific and supplies no label-invariant structural certificate for when a realizable fixed-count, marginally balanced covariance kernel makes rank preservation solve every marginal instance.
literature_map.locator: BrennanEtAl2025IntegerProgramming, Introduction, equation (4), Sections 4--5, Theorem 1, and Conclusion.

literature_map.settled: Zhao and Ding derive \(\operatorname{Cov}_Z(\widehat\tau)=N^{-1}C\{\operatorname{diag}(S_{aa}/e_a)-S\}C^{\mathsf T}\) for arbitrary multi-arm contrasts under complete randomization.
literature_map.open_boundary: They use conservative covariance estimators and do not optimize the unidentified cross-arm covariance completion.
literature_map.locator: ZhaoDing2023MultiarmedAdjustment, Section 2.1, equation (1), and the complete-randomization covariance display.

literature_map.settled: Tchen's concordance inequalities imply that comonotone coupling maximizes expectations of supermodular objectives with fixed marginals.
literature_map.open_boundary: This probability theorem does not map experimental contrast geometry into a checkable risk cone or characterize universal Loewner dominance.
literature_map.locator: Tchen1980GivenMarginals, Theorem 2.1 and the fixed-marginal supermodular-order discussion.

literature_map.settled: Gao, Ge, and Qian represent general quadratic cross-world identified sets by multi-marginal optimal transport and establish plug-in rates.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their general optimizer is numerical; they do not isolate the design-induced quadratic costs for which the comonotone plan is universally optimal.
literature_map.locator: GaoGeQian2025MultipleWorlds, Introduction, Section 2, Theorem 1 and its proof sketch, quadratic extension, and Discussion.

literature_map.settled: Laurent and Seminaroti prove identity-permutation optimality when a Robinson similarity and Robinson dissimilarity are paired and one matrix is Toeplitz.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their theorem is sufficient, concerns two matrices, and gives a counterexample when Toeplitz structure is removed; it does not characterize the multi-block causal kernel cone.
literature_map.locator: LaurentSeminaroti2015RobinsonianQAP, Introduction, Lemma 3, Theorems 4--5, proof decomposition, and the non-Toeplitz counterexample.

literature_map.settled: Imbens and Menzel show that isotone imputation yields a least-favourable two-arm limiting experiment and conservative asymptotic coverage.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their construction does not determine when one completion is jointly least favourable for several contrasts.
literature_map.locator: ImbensMenzel2021CausalBootstrap, Introduction, causal-bootstrap construction, Lemma 1, Proposition 1, and large-sample coverage argument.

novelty_justification: {"closest_results":"The closest causal result is Aronow, Green, and Lee's two-arm comonotone sharp variance bound. The closest general computational result is Brennan et al.'s integer-program completion. Tchen supplies the classical supermodular-order ingredient, and Laurent--Seminaroti supply a structured quadratic-assignment analogue.","consumer_delta":"A causal-bootstrap analyst can decide in \\(O(K^2)\\) time whether sorting once is a valid least-favourable completion for a stated covariance loss, audit the decision with exact \\(K=3,N=6\\) calculations, and learn when no single rank completion can conservatively represent a multi-contrast covariance matrix. The open extension asks for an analogous label-free certificate only on covariance tensors realizable by fixed-count, marginally balanced assignment laws.","non_subsumption":"The proposal does not claim a new rearrangement inequality. Its first theorem derives the causal graph-Laplacian cone from the design covariance formula and proves necessity by marginally isolated binary witnesses, including an explicit non-Laplacian loss calculation. Its second theorem classifies all contrast matrices for which every rank-one scalarization lies in that cone. The nonexchangeable extension is not posed over arbitrary arrays: its exact probability-simplex moment representation, covariance identities, feasibility constraints, and unit-relabeling quotient define the open domain.","precise_gap":"No located source characterizes the exact set of scalarizations \\((C,W)\\) for which common ranks maximize complete-randomization covariance for every armwise marginal collection, nor the stronger boundary at which the entire contrast covariance matrix is universally dominated in Loewner order. For nonexchangeable balanced designs, no located source characterizes which realizable assignment-covariance orbits meet the universal identity-optimal cone or gives a polynomial recognition and separation certificate."}
